finalText:
Root cause chain, timestamps UTC:

**02:14:07** — `[api]` lose redis connection: `ECONNREFUSED 10.0.0.12:6379`. Cache layer degrade, fall back to direct store read.

**02:14:08 onward** — cache miss storm start, store get flood direct read, timeout after 5000ms every request. Queue depth climb steady: 52 → 500+ over next 17min, never recover.

**02:14:07–02:31:26** — redis reconnect retry every ~140s, all 13 attempt fail (attempt 0 through 12), same ECONNREFUSED. Redis never come back whole window.

**02:31:44** — worker-2 heap out of memory (backlog pile too big, GC choke).

**02:31:45** — supervisor restart worker-2 (exit code 134 = SIGABRT from OOM).

**02:31:52** — api itself unresponsive, supervisor kill whole process group. Service down. Log end here.

Root cause: redis at 10.0.0.12:6379 drop, never reconnect for 17+ minutes. No circuit breaker or backpressure on direct-store fallback, so request queue grow unbounded (52→568+) instead of shed load, eventually OOM kill worker then whole service.

Fix direction: add circuit breaker/backpressure when store overload (reject or shed excess instead of queue infinite), separately need investigate why redis at .12 unreachable that long.
